course.title: International Integrated Science 9
course.subtitle: Life, Matter, Energy and Earth Systems
course.credit_recommendation: 1 high-school science credit, subject to local law and school policy
course.mapping_status: International benchmark synthesis. Jurisdiction-specific review is required before formal standards or credit reporting.
course.assessment_principle: Every scored item must have one definitive, defensible answer or an explicit evidence-based rubric.

mastery_scale.label: Beginning
mastery_scale.description: Needs direct instruction, modeling, and supported practice.

mastery_scale.label: Developing
mastery_scale.description: Shows partial understanding with inconsistent application or evidence.

mastery_scale.label: Proficient
mastery_scale.description: Applies scientific ideas and practices accurately in familiar contexts.

mastery_scale.label: Mastered
mastery_scale.description: Explains, transfers, evaluates, and applies learning in unfamiliar contexts.

units.title: Readiness, Laboratory Safety & Scientific Habits
units.big_idea: Safe, ethical, careful scientific work begins with habits that protect people, evidence, organisms, communities, and environments.

units.title: Scientific Inquiry, Measurement & Evidence
units.big_idea: Scientific explanations become stronger when questions are testable, measurements are reliable, and claims are supported by transparent evidence.

units.title: Cells & the Organization of Life
units.big_idea: Cells are organized systems whose structures and processes make life possible across many scales.
objectives: Explain cell theory and evaluate evidence that living organisms are cellular
Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells without treating either as inferior
Relate major cell structures to their contributions within the whole-cell system
Use microscope scale, image size, actual size, and magnification calculations
Model selective permeability, diffusion, osmosis, and active transport
Explain how surface-area-to-volume ratio constrains cell size and exchange
Connect specialized cells to tissues, organs, and organ systems
Describe photosynthesis and cellular respiration as linked matter and energy processes
Evaluate strengths and limitations of diagrams, models, and microscope images
framework_tags: NGSS: cells, structure and function, hierarchical organization, scientific modeling
Cambridge Biology: organisation of organisms; movement into and out of cells; practical skills
Australian Curriculum: cells, organ systems, inquiry, data interpretation, model evaluation
IB MYP Sciences: knowing and understanding; processing and evaluating
PISA scientific literacy: explain phenomena, evaluate inquiry, interpret evidence

units.title: Body Systems & Homeostasis
units.big_idea: Organ systems interact through feedback and transport processes to maintain stable internal conditions.
objectives: Explain homeostasis as dynamic regulation within functional limits
Model negative feedback using receptors, coordinating centers, effectors, and responses
Trace transport of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, water, ions, hormones, heat, and wastes
Relate structures of the circulatory, respiratory, digestive, urinary, nervous, endocrine, and immune systems to function
Analyze safe physiological-response data without using it to diagnose health conditions
Explain thermoregulation, blood-glucose regulation, and water balance as interacting feedback systems
Compare rapid neural signaling with slower endocrine signaling
Evaluate system models, health claims, uncertainty, and personal-data ethics
framework_tags: NGSS HS-LS1-2 and HS-LS1-3: interacting systems, feedback, and homeostasis
Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 (2026–2028): nutrition, transport, gas exchange, excretion, coordination, immunity, and practical skills
Australian Curriculum Year 9: coordinated and interdependent body systems responding to environmental change
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: systems, inquiry, evidence, evaluation, and impacts

units.title: Cell Division, Reproduction & Inheritance
units.big_idea: Genetic information is copied, expressed, reshuffled, and inherited, producing both continuity and variation.
objectives: Relate DNA, genes, alleles, chromosomes, and genomes across biological scales
Model the cell cycle, DNA replication, mitosis, cytokinesis, growth, repair, and differentiation
Explain how cell-cycle regulation limits uncontrolled division and why simplified cancer models have boundaries
Compare asexual and sexual reproduction in terms of continuity, variation, costs, and context
Model meiosis, homologous chromosome separation, crossing over, independent assortment, and fertilization
Use genotype, phenotype, dominance, codominance, incomplete dominance, and probability accurately
Construct and interpret monohybrid crosses while recognizing that probability does not guarantee family outcomes
Explain mutation and recombination as sources of variation and environment as an influence on trait expression
Evaluate genetic claims, technologies, privacy, consent, uncertainty, and the history of genetic misuse
framework_tags: NGSS HS-LS1-4 and HS-LS3-1–3: mitosis, differentiation, DNA and chromosomes, variation, statistics, and probability
Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610/0970 (2026–2028): reproduction, inheritance, variation, selection, and mathematical/practical skills
Australian Curriculum V9 Year 10 AC9S10U01: mitosis, meiosis, chromosomes, DNA, genes, and Mendelian inheritance
IB MYP Sciences: models, systems, patterns, inquiry, processing, evaluation, and impacts
PISA scientific literacy: explain phenomena, interpret data, evaluate evidence, and communicate uncertainty

units.title: Ecosystems, Evolution & Biodiversity
units.big_idea: Living systems depend on interconnected energy, matter, populations, environments, inherited variation, historical evidence, and responsible stewardship.
objectives: Distinguish organism, population, community, ecosystem, habitat, niche, and biotic and abiotic factors using direct observations
Construct and interpret food chains, food webs, trophic levels, biomass and energy pyramids, and ecological-efficiency calculations
Explain that energy flows through ecosystems while matter cycles through biological, atmospheric, hydrological, and geological reservoirs
Analyze real population records using density, trends, limiting factors, carrying capacity, uncertainty, and alternative explanations
Compare competition, predation, herbivory, mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, disturbance, succession, and resilience
Measure biodiversity using richness, abundance, evenness, sampling design, and a diversity index while protecting sensitive species locations
Explain natural selection as population change across generations involving inherited variation and differential reproductive success
Distinguish microevolution, speciation, and macroevolution, and state what has been directly observed versus historically reconstructed
Evaluate fossils, anatomy, biogeography, genetics, and dating evidence by separating specimens and measurements from classification and ancestry inference
Represent creation, intelligent-design, evolutionary-creation, and naturalistic interpretations accurately while distinguishing empirical, historical, philosophical, and theological claims
Design evidence-based biodiversity conservation or restoration actions that address safety, access, community knowledge, justice, uncertainty, and monitoring
framework_tags: NGSS HS-LS2-1–8: population data, matter and energy, interactions, resilience, group behavior, biodiversity, and design
NGSS HS-LS4-1–6: evidence, variation, natural selection, adaptation, environmental change, and biodiversity solutions
Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610/0970 (2026–2028): variation and selection; organisms and environment; human influences and conservation
Australian Curriculum V9 AC9S9U01 and AC9S10U02: ecosystem interdependence and evidence for evolution by natural selection
Academy enrichment: observation–inference–worldview distinctions and respectful comparative origins literacy

units.title: Atomic Structure & Periodic Patterns
units.big_idea: The arrangement and behavior of subatomic particles explain patterns in elements, isotopes, ions, and materials.

units.title: Bonding, Chemical Reactions & Matter
units.big_idea: Atoms rearrange during chemical reactions while matter and charge are conserved.

units.title: Motion, Forces & Energy
units.big_idea: Changes in motion and energy can be measured, modeled, predicted, and engineered.

units.title: Electricity, Waves & Information
units.big_idea: Electrical and wave systems transfer energy and information through patterns that can be measured and controlled.

units.title: Earth Systems & Biogeochemical Cycles
units.big_idea: Earth functions through interacting geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and cryosphere systems.

units.title: Dynamic Earth, Climate & Space
units.big_idea: Evidence from rocks, hazards, climate records, planetary motion, and light reveals a changing Earth within a larger universe.

units.title: Sustainable Engineering Capstone
units.big_idea: Engineering uses scientific evidence, criteria, constraints, testing, and revision to improve solutions while accounting for human and environmental consequences.
